stories.title: Thitikul Wins CME Three-Peat, Passes Sorenstam Career Earnings Record

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Jeeno Thitikul just won the CME Group Tour Championship for the THIRD year in a row.

No one has ever done that at this event. She also passed Annika Sorenstam's all-time LPGA earnings record. Final round 65. 2-shot win over Aki Iwai.

Historic. #LPGA

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Thitikul: 3 CME championships in a row. 5 LPGA titles in 2026. Career earnings past Annika Sorenstam's record.

Nelly Korda needed the win for the LPGA Hall of Fame. She finished 3rd.

Jeeno is in a different stratosphere. #LPGA

research.facts:
Thitikul CME Three-Peat
**Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Tournament: 2026 CME Group Tour Championship
- Venue: Tiburón Golf Club, Naples, Florida
- Winner: Atthaya "Jeeno" Thitikul
- Final round: 7-under 65
- Winning margin: 2 shots over Aki Iwai
- Nelly Korda finished 3rd, 4 shots back
- First player in CME event history to win three consecutive times
- First LPGA player since Inbee Park (2013-15, Women's PGA Championship) to win same tournament 3 straight years
- Prize: $4 million (largest in women's golf)
- Fifth LPGA title of 2026
- Career earnings after win: $24,292,858 — surpasses Annika Sorenstam's LPGA career earnings record

stories.title: LIV Golf Bankruptcy Disclosure Hearing Tuesday — Wind-Down Begins

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
LIV Golf's bankruptcy disclosure hearing is tomorrow (Tuesday, Nov 24) in New Jersey.

The court will consider beginning the wind-down of the $5B league. Meanwhile the PGA Tour is fighting a sweeping creditor subpoena — calling it a "desperate fishing expedition."

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The end of LIV Golf moves through court tomorrow.

Creditors want PGA Tour financial documents — revenue, media rights, player pay. The Tour says no. Judge Kaplan will sort it out.

The $5B experiment is almost over.

LIV Golf Bankruptcy Hearing Nov 24
**Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Hearing date: Tuesday, November 24, 2026 (confirmed as Tuesday from multiple sources; Nov 24 is Tuesday)
- Court: New Jersey (Bankruptcy Judge Michael Kaplan)
- Purpose: Conditionally approve LIV Golf's disclosure statement — begins wind-down phase
- LIV filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy: September 8, 2026
- BC Partners deal fell through; Saudi PIF stopped funding April 2026
- Liquidation target: January 2027
- PGA Tour subpoena: creditors demanded 18 categories of Tour documents (revenue, sponsorships, media rights, player compensation)
- Tour called it a "desperate fishing expedition"
- Creditors requested Tour documents by December 4

stories.title: Blades Brown's Historic PGA Tour Win — Youngest in 95 Years

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Reminder: Blades Brown, 19, won the World Wide Technology Championship on Nov 8 — the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years.

He rallied from 7 shots back with a 63 and won in a playoff.

He now has an invite to The Players Championship. That's wild.

research.facts:
Blades Brown Youngest PGA Tour Winner 95 Years
**Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Winner: Blades Brown (19 years old)
- Tournament: World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal, Los Cabos, Mexico
- Date: November 8, 2026
- Final round: 9-under 63 (rallied from 7-shot deficit)
- Won in playoff: birdie on second playoff hole over Ben James
- Record: youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
- Previous record: Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open at 18 (1931)
- Earned: spot at The Players Championship, PGA Championship invitation next year
- Turned pro as a teenager; earned 2027 PGA Tour card via top 20 Korn Ferry Tour finish
